topic: How the shipping container changed the world
hook: A plain steel box made your stuff cheaper.
visual_style: Photorealistic cinematic film still, real materials and textures, shallow depth of field, salty harbor air, golden hour light on rust-red steel and grey water
world: American harbors from a crowded 1950s dockside to a giant modern container terminal, golden hour light
through_line: one rust-red steel container, from a 1956 deck to a towering modern stack

cast.Trucker: a man in his 40s in a 1950s grey suit and grey fedora, square jaw, sleeves rolled up

props.Container: a plain corrugated steel shipping container painted rust red, no markings, letters or logos

cta: Share this with someone who loves how the world really works.

captions.hook_line: A plain steel box quietly made almost everything you own cheaper 📦
captions.body: In 1956, trucking entrepreneur Malcom McLean's ship Ideal X carried 58 containers from Newark to Houston. Loading loose cargo by hand cost about $5.83 a ton; loading containers cost around 16 cents. Standard boxes that move from ship to train to truck unopened rewired global trade.
captions.comment_prompt: What's the most surprising thing you think came to you in a container?

youtube_title: The Steel Box That Made Everything Cheaper

blocks.narration: A plain steel box made your stuff cheaper. Almost everything you own rode in one, and the idea is barely seventy years old.

blocks.narration: Before the nineteen fifties, ships were loaded by hand, sack by sack and crate by crate, for days on end.

blocks.narration: Then a trucking boss named Malcom McLean had a thought. Why not lift the whole box onto the ship?

blocks.narration: In nineteen fifty-six, his ship sailed with fifty-eight of them. Loading costs fell from nearly six dollars a ton to sixteen cents.

blocks.narration: Today, the biggest ships carry them by the thousands. Look around you. Almost everything you own came in one.
